cards.title: What a video editor actually does — storytelling, not flashy transitions!
cards.takeaway: An editor decides WHAT the viewer sees and hears, in WHAT order, and for HOW LONG so the story feels clear and engaging.
cards.body:
Beginners think editing means spinning star transitions every 3 seconds. Real editors know better!

**Video editing is invisible storytelling:**
- Cutting dead pauses, 'umms', and shaky mistakes.
- Choosing the clearest angle and best emotional reaction.
- Pacing sound, visuals, and captions so viewers watch to the very last second.

cards.title: Before touching the timeline: Ingest → Organise → Log → Backup
cards.takeaway: Professional editors ALWAYS start with four calm steps in order: Ingest, Organise, Log, and Backup — BEFORE making a single cut!
cards.body:
Never drag files straight off a phone cable or SD card into CapCut/Premiere! Follow the first **4 stages of the 10-stage post-production workflow** in order:
1. **Ingest:** Copy all raw camera/phone clips and audio into your project folder on disk.
2. **Organise:** Sort into tidy folders (`01_Footage`, `02_Audio`, `03_Graphics`, `04_Exports`).
3. **Log:** Watch clips quickly, rename/tag the best takes, and note unusable shots.
4. **Backup:** Copy the folder onto a second drive or cloud (**'One copy is no copy!'**).

check.prompt: What are the FIRST FOUR stages of the professional post-production workflow, in order?

choices.text: Colour grade → Sound effects → Captions → Thumbnail
Film → Post straight to TikTok → Rename later

check.hint: Bring files in (Ingest), put in folders (Organise), review/label takes (Log), make a second safe copy (Backup)!
check.explanation: Spot on! Ingest → Organise → Log → Backup keeps every project fast, tidy, and crash-proof before cutting begins.

cards.title: 'One copy is no copy' — protect client footage like gold!
cards.takeaway: NEVER format an SD card or delete phone clips right after copying to one laptop — wait until a verified SECOND backup exists!
cards.body:
Why do pros repeat **'One copy is no copy'**?
Imagine shooting a client's wedding, copying clips to your laptop, wiping your phone/SD card immediately, and then your laptop hard drive fails that night. You cannot re-shoot a wedding!

- Keep **at least two separate copies** (e.g. Laptop SSD + External Drive / Cloud) and verify the clips play **before** deleting originals from your phone or memory card.

cards.title: Aspect Ratios & Resolution — matching TikTok vs. YouTube
cards.takeaway: Use vertical 9:16 for TikTok/Reels/Shorts, widescreen 16:9 for YouTube, and match your project resolution (1080p) to your delivery target!
cards.body:
Set your project settings **before** editing so you never have to re-layout titles later:
- **`9:16` (Vertical, `1080 × 1920`):** Full-screen phone vertical for **TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts**.
- **`16:9` (Horizontal Widescreen, `1920 × 1080`):** Standard landscape for **YouTube, TVs, and laptops**.
- **`1:1` or `4:5`:** Square/portrait feed posts.

*Watch out:* If you shoot sharp **1080p** video for YouTube and accidentally set your timeline project to **720p**, you throw away sharpness and your final export looks soft!

check.prompt: Which aspect ratio is built for full-screen vertical videos on TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts?
check.hint: Hold your phone upright — narrow width (9) and tall height (16)!
check.explanation: Exactly! 9:16 (`1080 × 1920`) fills a vertical phone screen edge-to-edge on TikTok, Reels, and Shorts.

cards.title: Never lose quality or client trust on Day 1
cards.takeaway: Keep raw files untouched (non-destructive editing), match 1080p timeline settings, and verify two backups before wiping cards.
cards.body: Modern video editors are **non-destructive**: trimming a clip on the timeline never cuts your original video file on disk — unless you delete or move the source folder! Keep all assets inside your numbered project folder from start to finish.

check.prompt: True or False: It is safe to delete original wedding footage from your phone the exact second you finish copying it onto one laptop.

choices.text: True — one laptop copy never fails
False — 'one copy is no copy'; verify playback and keep a second independent backup before deleting originals

check.hint: What happens if that single laptop gets stolen or its drive fails tonight?
check.explanation: Correct — False! Always keep at least two verified copies in separate places before clearing camera cards or phone storage.
